```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

A `project_sensitive` project splits every data and output folder into
`private/` (gitignored, never shared) and `public/` (reviewed, safe to
commit). This notebook treats the participant-level study data as
identifiable, works with it in `private/`, and moves only aggregated results
to `public/`. Rendered notebooks go to `outputs/private/notebooks/`, both from
`quarto render` (`_quarto.yml`) and from Framework's render settings.

## The private/public layout

`project_info()` shows both halves. The `save_*()` functions write to private
by default and to public only with `public = TRUE`.

```{r}
project_info()
```

## Identifiable data goes in inputs/private

The participant and survey extracts land in `inputs/private/raw/`.

```{r}
shared_csv <- "../../shared/csv"
file.copy(file.path(shared_csv, "participants.csv"), "inputs/private/raw/participants.csv", overwrite = TRUE)
file.copy(file.path(shared_csv, "survey.csv"), "inputs/private/raw/survey.csv", overwrite = TRUE)
```

Register them in the catalog. `data_add()` names each file from its folder,
so `inputs/private/raw/participants.csv` becomes
`inputs.private.raw.participants`.

```{r}
data_add("inputs/private/raw/participants.csv")
data_add("inputs/private/raw/survey.csv")
data_list()
```

`data_info()` flags the private location.

```{r}
data_info("inputs.private.raw.survey")$private
```

## From private rows to public aggregates

Participant rows stay private. The public output is a site-by-arm summary of
survey stress scores, with cells under 10 participants suppressed so no small
group can be singled out.

```{r}
participants <- data_read("inputs.private.raw.participants")
survey <- data_read("inputs.private.raw.survey")
sites <- db_query("SELECT site_id, site_name FROM sites", "study")

stress_by_site <- participants |>
  inner_join(survey, by = "participant_id") |>
  inner_join(sites, by = "site_id") |>
  group_by(site_name, treatment) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_stress = round(mean(stress_score, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Small-cell suppression: hide the mean, and the count, for tiny groups
  mutate(
    mean_stress = if_else(n < 10, NA_real_, mean_stress),
    n = if_else(n < 10, NA_integer_, n)
  )
stress_by_site
```

Dot notation picks the folder: `inputs.public.final.*` saves to
`inputs/public/final/`, and a `.csv` ending saves it as CSV.

```{r}
data_save(stress_by_site, "inputs.public.final.stress_by_site.csv")
```

## Private by default, public on request

A table of individual high-stress participants is for the study team only, so
it goes to the private tables folder.

```{r}
high_stress <- survey |> filter(stress_score >= 30) |> select(participant_id, stress_score, completed_on)
save_table(high_stress, "high_stress_participants")
```

The aggregate table and its figure are safe to share.

```{r}
save_table(stress_by_site, "stress_by_site", public = TRUE)

stress_plot <- ggplot(stress_by_site, aes(site_name, mean_stress, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean stress score", fill = NULL)
save_figure(stress_plot, "stress_by_site", public = TRUE, width = 7, height = 4)
```

```{r}
result_list()[, c("name", "type", "public")]
```

## What git ignores

`git check-ignore` reports which rule ignores a path. Every `private/` path is
ignored; the public files and the code are not, so they'd be committed.

```{r}
paths <- c(
  "inputs/private/raw/participants.csv",
  "outputs/private/tables/high_stress_participants.csv",
  "inputs/public/final/stress_by_site.csv",
  "outputs/public/tables/stress_by_site.csv",
  "notebooks/01-private-and-public-data.qmd",
  "framework.db",
  ".env"
)
ignored <- vapply(paths, function(path) {
  status <- system2("git", c("check-ignore", "-q", path))
  status == 0
}, logical(1))
data.frame(path = paths, ignored = ignored, row.names = NULL)
```

The rules come from this project's `.gitignore`.

```{r}
gitignore <- readLines(".gitignore")
gitignore[grepl("private|sensitive", gitignore) & !startsWith(gitignore, "#")]
```

## Encryption

Framework doesn't encrypt data files. Private data is protected by the folder
layout, `.gitignore`, the audit, and the publish guard below. An `encrypted`
argument isn't accepted.

```{r}
#| error: true
data_save(participants, "inputs.private.intermediate.participants", encrypted = TRUE)
```

## Security audit

`git_security_audit()` checks gitignore coverage of the private folders,
tracked private files, data in git history, tracked secrets, and data files
outside the configured folders.

```{r}
audit <- git_security_audit()
audit$summary
```

Now simulate a slip: someone exports participant rows to the top of
`outputs/`, outside both `private/` and `public/`. The audit flags it as a data
file outside the configured folders, and `git check-ignore` confirms git would
pick it up.

```{r}
data_save(participants, "outputs/participants_export.csv")
system2("git", c("check-ignore", "-q", "outputs/participants_export.csv")) == 0
```

```{r}
audit <- git_security_audit(check_git_history = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
audit$summary
audit$findings$orphaned_files[, c("path", "extension")]
```

Clean up the slip.

```{r}
unlink("outputs/participants_export.csv")
```

## Publishing guards

Publishing checks the path first. A file whose path contains "private" stops
in a non-interactive session (and asks first in the console) unless you pass
`include_private = TRUE`.

```{r}
#| error: true
publish("outputs/private/tables/high_stress_participants.csv")
```

## Pre-commit hook

The `data_security` hook blocks commits that track private data or secrets.
It is off by default, even in a sensitive project; turn it on with
`git_hooks_enable("data_security")` and `git_hooks_install()` in a project
that is its own git repository. Here the project sits inside the shared test
repo, so installing refuses.

```{r}
git_hooks_list()
```

```{r}
#| error: true
git_hooks_install()
```
